newsitem.title: UK: Lifters agree to pay more for Algeria's Sahara.
newsitem.headline: Lifters agree to pay more for Algeria's Sahara.

text.p: Lifters of Algerian Saharan blend crude have agreed to pay a premium of 53 cents to dated Brent for August contract barrels, some 10-15 cents more than in July, traders said.

Lifters hoped to negotiate the price down to around 40-45 cents over the benchmark blend, closer to the 39 to 40 cent premium in July, but were disappointed and resolved instead into limit their uptake.
"I think everyone is going to agree to 53 cents but people have reduced their requirements because they think it's too expensive," said one trader.

One Mediterranean refiner took only one out of a possible four cargoes. Most believed Algerian state oil company Sonatrach would be left with barrels that could be picked up more cheaply later from the spot market.
"When Iraqi barrels appear then we are sure the numbers will come off," said one.
